messages:
Olivia (Support): Hey team — customer 'StreamlineAI' opened a P1: their CI deploys to Dedicated keep failing with 403 when calling the Redwood API during the post-deploy smoke step. Happens ~30% of runs, started yesterday after we rolled out model-cache endpoint. Logs attached below.

mike.dev: Can you paste the error from the CI logs? 403 usually means missing scope or wrong audience.

Olivia (Support): Sure — here's the snippet from their pipeline:

```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/model-cache/purge 403 Forbidden
response: {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token lacks scope 'cache:purge'"}
ci-job: pipeline/deploy/step-post-deploy
service_account: sa-ci-deployer@streamline-prod
token_aud: https://auth.redwood-inference.com
exp: 1679998940
```

ashley.sre: That error is pretty explicit. Did Streamline recently change the service-account scopes template? Could also be ephemeral token TTL expired between mint and call (but the error text is scope).

Olivia (Support): They say nothing changed on their side, but their pipeline image was updated last week. If the token is minted with a scope whitelist from our OIDC app, maybe the image uses an older token helper.

sam.devex: Quick repro steps I asked customer to run locally:
```
# replicate: mint token via OIDC helper
$ oidc-helper mint --sa sa-ci-deployer@streamline-prod --scopes openid email profile
# call purge (should be 403)
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/model-cache/purge
```
They confirmed that minting without cache:purge yields 403, adding cache:purge succeeds. So the pipeline is not requesting the new scope.

mike.dev: Why would the pipeline omit the scope sometimes (30% flakiness)? Maybe there are two token minting paths in their monorepo: one legacy shell script and one new node helper. One might request scopes from environment var and another fall back to default scopes.

Olivia (Support): They confirmed there are two helpers. The deploy step uses the new helper, the smoke test uses a helper embedded in a sidecar that still uses the old default scopes.

ashley.sre: Ok that's the cause. Short-term mitigation: add RBAC to give sa-ci-deployer the aggregate role that includes cache:purge so both token variants work while they fix the helper. Long-term: require explicit scope assertion in CI and add a unit test that validates token scopes before deploy.

security-bot: Reminder: granting broad roles is allowed only as temporary mitigation. Please add a ticket to remove the temporary permission within 7 days and document the justification.

sam.devex: Proposed immediate steps for Support -> Customer guide: 1) Add `cache:purge` to the scope request in their sidecar config: `OIDC_SCOPES=openid,email,cache:purge` 2) Or as fallback, run `redwoodctl grant-role sa-ci-deployer redwood.cache.purger --ttl 72h` (example command in org docs).

mike.dev: To prevent recurrence we should:
- Add server-side telemetry to detect when a token is missing common scopes and emit a specific metric (auth.missing_scope.cache_purge)
- Add a CI smoke job on our end that uses a variety of helper implementations to mint tokens and call critical endpoints.

Olivia (Support): Customer applied the quickfix and confirmed deploys are passing now. They're going to update the sidecar image to request the correct scopes and will remove the temporary role.

ashley.sre: Follow-up items for us:
1) Create an internal KB entry for "CI sidecars and scope drift" with repro, quickfix, and recommended permanent fix (include `redwoodctl` examples and least-privilege role bindings).
2) Add an alert in Console that surfaces repeated 403s with body containing `insufficient_scope` and the endpoint name.
3) Add a note to Dedicated onboarding docs that adding new endpoints requiring scopes can cause older CI helpers to break.

sam.devex: I'll draft the KB and a tiny test harness for dev teams to validate scope requests.

security-bot: Logged ticket SEC-2026-114 (temporary permission request) and TAX-2026-09 (audit note).

mike.dev: One extra nuance — the customer's tokens show `exp` far in the future in their logs above (maybe misconfigured clock); we should remind teams to check system clock and token TTLs as part of the KB.

Olivia (Support): Marking this thread resolved from support POV — customer has working deploys. Leaving follow-ups for eng/sre/devex as action items. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
